sections.heading: Background and Scope
sections.body: This report page summarizes the transfer pricing analysis for fiscal year ended 31 December 2025 concerning intercompany transactions between AlphaTech US, Inc. and its EMEA and APAC distribution and service affiliates. The covered entities include AlphaTech Germany GmbH, AlphaTech Singapore Pte. Ltd., and AlphaTech Australia Pty Ltd. The analysis evaluates charges for software licensing, centralized R&D cost allocations, and shared services support to determine compliance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines (2022 edition). The objective is to demonstrate that the pricing outcomes reflect arm’s length conditions.

Management affirms that the pricing policies were applied consistently throughout the fiscal year.

structure.heading: Intercompany Transaction Overview and OECD Arm’s Length Delineation (FY2025)
text_content: **Intercompany Transaction Overview and OECD Arm’s Length Delineation (FY2025)**

This analysis covers intercompany transactions between AlphaTech US, Inc. and AlphaTech Ireland Ltd. for FY2025 (1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025). Under the Intercompany Services Agreement dated 15 March 2023, AlphaTech US, Inc. provided contract R&D services to AlphaTech Ireland Ltd. Total FY2025 intercompany charges documented in this study equal USD 128.6 million. Charges comprise direct project costs, allocated shared services, and a contractual markup. Invoices were issued monthly and posted in the general ledger in accordance with internal billing policies.

Applying OECD arm’s length delineation, the economically relevant transaction is contract R&D services performed by AlphaTech US. Functional analysis shows AlphaTech US delivered laboratory and engineering activities and owned project‑level development IP, while AlphaTech Ireland retained commercialization risk and market functions. Cost allocation reflects AlphaTech US bearing roughly 90% of direct project execution costs, with AlphaTech Ireland funding market entry expenditures. Contract terms and actual conduct were examined to ensure the allocation of functions, risks and assets aligns with documented transactional behavior.

Contemporaneous documentation supports the FY2025 delineation and pricing of the contract R&D relationship. Internal records reconcile USD 128.6 million of FY2025 intercompany charges to monthly invoices, project cost ledgers and the Intercompany Services Agreement dated 15 March 2023. Supporting evidence includes time sheets, project budgets and IP development logs. Governance procedures require annual review of allocations, maintenance of comparability files and retention of records for statutory audit. These measures are designed to evidence compliance with OECD arm’s length principles and tax reporting obligations.
